localTips.title: Leave the default electricity tariff
localTips.why: Households still on the local supplier’s default tariff (Grundversorgung) pay around 40 ct/kWh, while the cheapest new-customer tariffs are around 30 ct/kWh.
tips: Find your yearly kWh on your last bill and compare tariffs on Check24 or Verivox.
Pick a tariff with a 12-month price guarantee and no prepayment.
Set a reminder to compare again before the first year ends, when bonuses run out.

pct.note: Derived from ~40.4 vs ~29.9 ct/kWh (StromAuskunft, Oct 2026) after standing charges; only for households in Grundversorgung or old contracts

localTips.title: Switch your gas supplier
localTips.why: Gas prices for new customers are well below the default tariff and many long-standing contracts.
tips: Compare gas tariffs with your yearly kWh from the last statement.
Check your monthly prepayment (Abschlag) matches your real use so you avoid a big back-payment.
Bleed radiators and turn the heating down 1°C; each degree saves about 6%.

pct.note: Estimate; gap between default (~13.6 ct) and new-customer (~9–12 ct) gas prices in 2026 sources

localTips.title: Ask for a Deutschlandticket Job
localTips.why: If your employer pays at least 25% of the Deutschlandticket, the price drops a further 5%, so your share can fall well below €63.
tips: Ask HR whether they offer the Deutschlandticket Job.
Cancel single tickets and local monthly passes the Deutschlandticket already covers.
Check whether your state offers a cheaper student or social version.

pct.note: Estimate: employer pays ≥25% plus 5% discount; depends on the employer
